headline.title: Yields are the story, and they are being pushed from two directions at once. The 10-year hit 4.788%, its highest since Jan 14, 2025; the 30-year is 5.279%. Japan's 10-year JGB touched 3.00% for the first time since 1996 with Bessent publicly pressuring Tokyo to hike, and European 10-years jumped ~10bp. Underneath it, WTI +2.2% to ~$87.63 and Brent ~$91.93 after two tankers were struck near the Strait of Hormuz.
headline.summary: Higher discount rates plus higher energy input costs is what long-duration growth cannot absorb, and the tape shows it: SMH −2.1%, QQQ −1.4%, INTC −3.1%, AMD −2.5%, META −2.5%. Monday itself was thin and slightly red — Dow −374 to 53,186, S&P −0.3% to 7,686, Nasdaq −0.1% to 26,370 — but August still closed green, the Dow's fifth straight winning month at +2.1%, S&P ~+3%, Nasdaq ~+4%. ISM Manufacturing (seen ~55, prior 55.6) and JOLTS (seen ~7.3M) both land at 9:00am CT, and with September hike odds now 57-62%, ISM Prices Paid is the line that matters. Five report tonight — DELL, PANW, MDB, CRDO and GTLB — with implied moves of 10.4%, 9.3%, 15.9% and 11.7%.

overview: The prep sheet is a patience sheet today, and the tape agrees with it. “Be very patient and secure profits before swinging overnight” at $50 risk, with Wednesday through Friday flagged as the main days this week — today is a setup session, not a swing-for-it session. The index plan is mechanical: data at 9:00am, then a 30-minute ORB, which is also the cleanest way to resolve the conflict sitting under the index. SPY and IWM printed real 2 Downs Monday and both trade below Monday's low; QQQ is a Failed 2D that premarket is voiding. Against that, Monday's block tape was index accumulation on the bid — SPY $3.5B and IVV $2.4B cumulative, the two largest lines on the whole board. Block money bought; option money paid for downside via a $2.3M QQQ $715P sweep. The single-name conviction is CVX: a 2-2-2 up on the daily with ATH at $214.69 overhead, and today's premarket already clears Monday's high to put the third leg in motion.

darkpool.note: Monday's block tape bought the index while the tape closed red, and that is the day's central conflict. The two largest lines on the entire board were SPY $3.5B and IVV $2.4B cumulative, both bid, and the single biggest print on the tape was IVV $1.3B bid AH, with SPY $1.2B, SPYM $1.0B and QQQ $358M behind it — index money crossing in size into the close even as futures pointed lower. The loudest single name went the other way: SNDK $2.8B cumulative ask, second on the whole board, plus a ~$500M print of its own. Ex-ETF the biggest single print was GOOGL $774M bid (with GOOG adding $500M bid) and it is down 1.2% this morning. Options money took the short side: the largest index ticket was a $2.3M QQQ $715P sweep and the largest single-name sweep a $1.6M NVDA $175P 11/20/26 — long-dated downside that reads as a hedge as easily as a bet. The largest block on either board was GS $800C 09/18/26 at $54.6M, a crossed floor ticket. Bid-side index ETFs against ask-side single names is a lean, not a verdict.
